When will they begin to produce caps if ever?
Do you have your mycelium in a Petrie dish? Is that what I see? Or have you put them in a substrate yet?

Okay, before caps appear you need to transfer your spawn to a substrate so it can grow, like a bag of sterile straw. Here is a good overview or you can just google oyster mushroom substrate preparation.

After about 2-3 weeks your substrate should be "pinning" or that's when you'll begin to see little caps appear.

If you need to slow your spawn down because you aren't quite ready to put it in the substrate (straw) yet, you can just set your Petri dishes in a fridge. They'll be fine for a week or more.

I was encouraged to share this story and song from this AskVoat post, I hope someone finds it amusing!

I used to work for a fairly large corporate real estate company in TX - they owned buildings different places, and leased out the space and whatnot, and I was part of the IT dept. at the corporate office. The company started out quite small, but by the time I started working there, they had property in several states, including a large building in downtown Dallas. There was still evidence of the company's initial "smallness", though, especially in places like the break room! It was stocked to the brim with food and snacks for the employees -- soft drinks, milk, cheese, cold cuts, peanut butter, bread, animal crackers, cookies, you name it!

Anyway, one day, I was at work quite early in the morning. Never one to shy away from taking advantage of the breakroom amenities, I trotted over to procure a drink. For some reason, apple juice seemed like a great choice that morning, so I grabbed a bottle, and strolled merrily back to my office. As I had the building to myself, I started singing about my newly-acquired apple juice, to the tune of the A-Team theme song. Right up until passed an open door and spotted a co-worker at her desk. Soooo, I did the most sensible thing you could do in 2006 - I made a LiveJournal Voice Post about how someone caught me singing a really dumb song at work! The post, of course, included a small sample of my singing. A few hours later, a friend commented that she needed better quality samples ( O_o ? ) so on lunch, I called her voicemail, re-sang the apple juice song and then read a bunch of stuff off of the label for good measure.

Before the sun had set that day, a new reply appeared on my LiveJournal post -- my magnum opus had been born unto the world! Enjoy!
